pr_body:
fixes #76422

It works on UDP & ICMP and  it seems to be silently ignored by kernel on TCP.

issue_context.title: The DontFragment SocketOptionName doesn't appear to work on macOS
issue_context.body:
### Description

Attempting to set DontFragment on a socket using `SetSocketOption` will cause a SocketException with error code 45, making it so that you can't have a socket that doesn't send fragmented packets without an exception occurring.

### Reproduction Steps

```cs
var socket = new Socket(AddressFamily.InterNetwork, SocketType.Dgram, ProtocolType.Udp);
socket.Bind(IPEndPoint.Parse("0.0.0.0:6500");
socket.SetSocketOption(SocketOptionLevel.IP, SocketOptionName.DontFragment, true);
```

### Expected behavior

The socket option to be correctly set.

### Actual behavior

```
Unhandled exception. System.Net.Sockets.SocketException (45): Operation not supported
   at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.UpdateStatusAfterSocketErrorAndThrowException(SocketError error, String callerName)
   at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.SetSocketOption(SocketOptionLevel optionLevel, SocketOptionName optionName, Int32 optionValue, Boolean silent)
   at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.SetSocketOption(SocketOptionLevel optionLevel, SocketOptionName optionName, Int32 optionValue)
   at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.SetSocketOption(SocketOptionLevel optionLevel, SocketOptionName optionName, Boolean optionValue)
```

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

None, that I know of. I cannot currently figure out how to actually set the raw option (it seems to be a boolean according to examples I've seen, but I've been having issues with passing in a read only span of bytes where it refuses to accept the byte span).

### Configuration

- NET 6.0.400
- macOS 11 (Big Sur)
- x64

### Other information

_No response_

AFAIK this is limitation of macOS. There is nothing .NET can really when kernel does not support it. We did some tricks to construct full IP header for `Ping` but that really does not work for TCP & UDP.

@vulppine do you know which macOS versions already support this flag? That would be very useful for us.

Triage: Reasonable to test and do. Not high pri.

> but I've been having issues with passing in a read only span of bytes where it refuses to accept the byte span

@vulppine can you share your code and error you get? `SetRawSocketOption()` is really just a wrapper around `setsockopt`, if there is an error, it should mean either incorrect usage, or an error reported by the OS.

> @vulppine do you know which macOS versions already support this flag? That would be very useful for us.
> 
> Triage: Reasonable to test and do. Not high pri.

It appears that macOS 11 and above may support `IP_DONTFRAG`, at least when it's set it using `setsockopt`. I'm not sure how it's handled in the kernel, as mentioned earlier by wfurt, there may be a limitation in macOS related to this.

> > but I've been having issues with passing in a read only span of bytes where it refuses to accept the byte span
> 
> @vulppine can you share your code and error you get? `SetRawSocketOption()` is really just a wrapper around `setsockopt`, if there is an error, it should mean either incorrect usage, or an error reported by the OS.

Actually, as it turns out, I was reading the exception incorrectly, and it's another unrelated exception further on. The flag seems to be set correctly when using `SetRawSocketOption`.

We have Tests for IPv6 and it is expected to throw as in general IPv6 does not fragment and forces PMTU discovery.
